text:
maria: Bringing up strix-11b (int4) on Dedicated canary. Seeing slow token throughput (~40 t/s) vs expected ~90 t/s, and intermittent OOMs when max_new_tokens > 512. Anyone seen this pattern before?
cheng: saw similar on the canary last night, slowgen spikes and then OOM on g3 nodes. stack looks like kernel scheduling stalls + KV cache growth.
ops-bot: ALERT: OOM on g03 (canary pool) 2024-03-15T21:12:03Z — container strix-canary-7 restarted.
indra: first guesses: (1) prefetch behavior + int4 layout causing fragmentation, (2) default max_new_tokens too high for slot reservation, (3) batching defaults too aggressive.
sam: are there perf dumps/metrics? rough numbers help decide whether it's memory fragmentation or pure allocation pressure.
maria: quick numbers from canary: median latency 380ms -> 900ms under load, t/s drops from 92 -> 38 at 75% load. OOMs happened at ~520 tokens in a tail request. link: https://internal.redwood/dash/strix11b/canary (internal)
cheng: paste of relevant logs: ```
[21:11:58] kv_cache_alloc: current_slots=246k target=250k
[21:12:01] kernel_queue: pending_tasks=12 stall_ms=34
[21:12:03] allocation failed: cudaMallocAsync returned OOM
[21:12:03] fallback: evicting kv entries -> 120MB freed
```
devon: propose quick mitigations to test on canary: set model.max_new_tokens_default=256, batch.max_batch_size=2, disable prefix_prefetching for this model, and enable slot_compactor with compact_threshold=0.25. Those should reduce fragmentation and reserve headroom.
indra: also try kv_prune_ratio=0.6 and lower slowstart_ramp to 0.35 for the runtime scheduler.
sam: please add a short perf regression check (QA prompts) before/after to ensure quality isn't regressing. we saw int4 sometimes adds subtle token distribution drift.
maria: will roll to canary now with changes: {"max_new_tokens_default": "256", "max_batch_size": "2", "prefix_prefetch": "off", "slot_compactor": "on(compact_threshold=0.25)", "kv_prune_ratio": "0.6", "slowstart_ramp": "0.35"}. kicking deploy.
ops-bot: DEPLOY STARTED: deploy/strix11b-canary-20240315-2135 by maria
cheng: +1 on the params. also keep trace sampling high for first 30m (trace_rate=0.2).
indra: reminder: add a small eval set (10 QA pairs, 5 summarization) to catch generation quality diffs. run eval before and after, log perplexity + exact-match.
maria: ran quick eval pre-change: EM=0.862, PPL=18.9. will run post-change and report.
(15m later)
maria: canary post-change: median throughput up to 78 t/s under same load, tail latency 420ms, no OOMs in last 40m. quality post-change: EM=0.854, PPL=19.3. small drop but within tolerances per product.
sam: small quality delta noted, but given cost/latency win I agree to continue. schedule a broader canary to 10% traffic.
devon: also add a short-lived mitigation: when request.max_new_tokens > 400, gate to a compatible model variant (e.g., strix-11b-compat-int8) until we have better slot guarantees.
maria: opened rollout ticket and canary -> 10% plan, added regression eval: https://internal.redwood/issue/STRX-231. will monitor. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: DEPLOY SUCCESS: deploy/strix11b-canary-20240315-2147 by maria
cheng: nice — follow-up actions: (1) add automatic max_new_tokens default per-model manifest, (2) hook into onboarding checklist to run fragmentation smoke test, (3) record kernel stall metrics in model profile.
indra: I'll add the fragmentation smoke test to the onboarding harness (small script that generates long tails + varying batch shapes).
maria: thanks team. will push changes to prod rollout doc and close the triage.
devon: leaving a note: if we see this pattern on other int4 models, we should consider a runtime conservative fallback for prefix_prefetch when slot_usage variance > 0.15.
sam: tagging for visibility: @product @reliability
maria: noted. closing thread for now, will reopen if regressions appear. :white_check_mark:
